transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, I'm here because... I've just been living with this constant mix of guilt, fear, and anger since my friend was killed. People kept telling me it would get easier with time, but it really hasn't eased up the way everyone seemed to think it would. It's just always there.
Do unwanted memories of what happened to your friend repeatedly pop into your mind?

Yes, they do. It really doesn't take much to bring it all back. Just hearing a crosswalk signal, or... or the growl of a truck going by. Even something as simple as seeing a walking-tour map can suddenly put the whole scene right back in my head. It comes back so sharply. I can just see my friend stepping off the curb, and it's like I'm right there again before I can even try to stop the memory.
Do you find yourself actively trying to avoid places, people, or activities that remind you of the accident?

Yes, I do. I go out of my way to avoid that intersection entirely. I just can't be near it. And... I've stopped signing up for most tours or even the neighborhood safety meetings. I just can't bear the conversations when they circle back to what happened there. It's too much.
Have you found yourself feeling constantly on guard, as if you're always watching out for danger?

Yes, very much so. Whenever I'm anywhere near traffic, I just... I find myself watching every single truck, the curbs, every pedestrian around me. It feels like it's my responsibility to catch the danger before it happens again. I just can't seem to turn that watchfulness off.
How long have you been experiencing these reactions since the accident happened?
Well, this has all been going on since my friend was killed on that walking tour. That was... about two years and three months ago now.
